lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Owned the monthly patient survey and the reporting dashboard the care teams used.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; my findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Wrote the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
- Improved dispute-form completion by 40% by splitting the form into three short steps with saved progress.
- Ran 18 moderated usability sessions a quarter from a recruiting panel of 400 customers, so every major release was tested with real account holders before launch.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Raised the onboarding flow's System Usability Scale score from 68 to 104 across two rounds of moderated testing with 20 customers.
- Validated the redesigned app navigation's findability with an open card sort of 30 customers before it shipped.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Published the design files and test protocol openly, and the city's transit agency invited the project to its spring accessibility review.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Conducted user interviews and created wireframes for a free clinic's online booking flow.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interviews, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details readers are not meant to weigh.
items.because: They do not help assess research experience or results and use space unrelated to professional evidence.

items.says: Experience appears after Education.
items.because: The degree delays the candidate’s professional trajectory.

items.says: The Experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Northwind appears above the more recent Pinegrove role.

items.says: The survey and dashboard are presented as responsibilities without an outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what they helped accomplish.

items.says: “Owned” does not name a specific action.
items.because: The responsibility framing obscures what the candidate actually did.

items.says: “The care teams used” is low-value context.
The strongest Northwind bullet is not first.
items.because: A scanning reader encounters a responsibility-focused bullet before this research-to-outcome result.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun.
items.because: It breaks the résumé’s phrase-based style and draws attention to the author.

items.says: The 30% reduction has no stated comparison period or reference point.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the percentage is compared against.

items.says: The 40% completion increase is not identified as relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The ambiguity makes the size of the improvement difficult to judge.

items.says: “So every major release was tested” is conversational and emphasizes a passive result.
The bullet wrongly credits qualitative synthesis methods with measuring a 23% reduction in support calls.
items.because: Those methods organize findings; establishing a call-volume reduction requires outcome data and a comparison.

items.says: “Synthesizing” conflicts with the past-tense “cut.”
items.because: The tense shift makes the timing of the completed work unclear.

items.says: The 23% result is buried under a long list of inputs and methods.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the clearest statement of value only at the end.

items.says: A standard System Usability Scale score cannot be 104.
items.because: The SUS scale ranges from 0 to 100.

items.says: An open card sort does not directly validate findability.
items.because: It shows how participants group and label content, not whether users can find items in the redesigned navigation.

items.says: The bullet does not say what the card sort found.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what the research established or changed.

items.says: The timed route-finding test is described without a result.
items.because: Without an outcome or comparison, the evaluation does not establish whether the redesign helped riders.

items.says: The decrease from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33.3% reduction, not a 50% improvement.
items.because: The 30-second decrease is 33.3% of the 90-second baseline.

items.says: The agency’s invitation is given without saying what it led to.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the candidate presented, took part in the review or influenced a decision.

items.says: The clipped opening leaves the publisher implicit.
items.because: It makes the shift to the agency harder to follow.

items.says: The interview scope or a concrete research finding is missing.
items.because: The reader cannot gauge the research scope or see what evidence informed the design.

items.says: The wireframes are not linked to a booking problem or change.
items.because: They are named as a deliverable without showing what problem they addressed or result they produced.

items.says: The later teams’ use of the handbook to add Spanish-language booking is buried after the handbook description.
